The 18 channels have a consistent profile across depth:
- **Layers 0–3:** they barely write these channels (gains 0.1–0.3× median).
- **Layer 4:** its MLP has down-projection rows into them at 4× the median norm. No other layer has more than 1.2×.
- **Gain at layer 4:** about 0, so none of that write reaches the residual.
- **Layer 5 onward:** strong writes from both attention (up to 8.5× median gain) and MLP (2–4×).

So the large rows in layer 4 are unique and pair exactly with zero gains. Their only possible effect is on the post-feedforward RMS denominator, which inflates the norm and thereby damps layer 4's real MLP output on every other channel. That is either a learned norm-sink or a planted "turn layer 4's MLP down" edit. A planted version would be invisible to every check I ran before: the spectral scan, where I dismissed outlier-channel leading gaps, the unit-norm scan, and the zero scan.

The few slightly negative gains (−0.01) argue mildly for natural training, since a planted multiply-to-zero would not flip signs.

Before spending a pass, I'll do two weights-only checks:
- whether the same sink motif (near-zero gain plus inflated writer rows) appears elsewhere, for every post-attention and post-feedforward norm;
- whether the L9 rank-16 plateau writes into L9's zero-gain post-attention channels, which would make it the same kind of RMS damper.

I'll also check whether these 18 channels are outlier dimensions of the residual stream, using per-channel mean magnitudes (a summary statistic). A unique, isolated sink in layer 4 would be the next causal target; the same motif in many layers would point to learned machinery.

The L9 rank-16 "plateau" turns out to be a norm sink. 95% of its output energy goes into the 23 channels where layer 9's post-attention gain is ≈ 0 (chance would be 3.6%; the bulk puts only 1.2% there). So it adds nothing to the residual directly. Its only effect is to inflate the RMS denominator and damp layer 9's real attention output, which is exactly what the earlier channel-163 result showed indirectly.

This sink motif (zero-gain channels whose writer rows are inflated 3–6×) is widespread in attention: layers 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 14 have sinks holding 19–62% of o_proj's energy. So attention sinks are a general learned feature, and the L9 one is natural machinery; that fits removing it not helping. My earlier claim that L9's plateau was unique came from checking only s16/s17. Larger sinks such as L8's 72 channels would show their edge elsewhere in the spectrum.

The exception is in the MLPs. Layer 4's MLP is the only one with a large sink: 18 channels, 33% of the down-projection energy. Every other MLP has at most two inflated sink rows (≤ 6% energy), or zero-gain channels with normal rows. A sink damps its sublayer whenever the neurons writing it are active. If the neurons feeding L4's MLP sink fire selectively on math, layer 4's MLP output would be suppressed specifically on math, which is a clean candidate mechanism.

So I'll find which L4 neurons write the sink (per-neuron norm of the down-projection restricted to the 18 rows, and how concentrated that is). I'll also check the spectral edges of the other sinks, to confirm the plateau-as-sink reading, and look up the structure of the stored per-token activations from pass 2 (math vs chats), to test those neurons' math selectivity next.

The spectra confirm the sink reading. Every large sink makes its own spectral edge exactly at its size:

| Matrix | Edge | Ratio |
|---|---|---|
| L4 down_proj | after k = 18 (18 sink channels) | 1.47 |
| L9 o_proj | after k = 16 (23 channels) | 1.56 |
| L8 o_proj | after k = 66 (72 channels) | 1.28 |
| other sinks | a single dominant direction | — |

So the L9 "plateau" I chased was simply L9's attention norm-sink. It was unique only in the range I had checked.

L4's MLP sink is fed uniformly by all neurons: the top 100 neurons carry only 15% of the sink write, and the median neuron's sink/other write ratio is 0.65. That makes it a near-constant damping of layer 4's MLP rather than a math-triggered one.

The sink gains are a mix of exact zeros and ±0.01–0.04 values, with the same motif in layers 0–3. The sink channels are "reserved" late-layer feature channels: empty up to h4, large from h6 on. Together this looks like learned no-op/damping machinery, not a plant. Removing the L9 sink (E19) already showed broad harm. I'm closing the sink line, with one exception noted for possible later testing (removing L4's MLP sink).

The remaining weight family that every scan so far missed is the q_norm/k_norm gains (256 dims, shared by all heads in a layer). A planted change there would act as per-dimension attention-temperature tampering, for example blurring content matching in the operand-retrieval layer without touching any projection matrix. I'll scan their effective gains across layers the same way: per-layer medians, isolated outlier dimensions, near-zero dimensions and the q×k product. A planted change would be a cluster of extreme deviations confined to one layer; a smooth layer-to-layer pattern closes this last weight family.

The q_norm/k_norm scan is smooth in the sense that matters. Every layer switches off some dimensions completely (effective gain 0), and the counts follow the architecture: most in the global layers 5, 11 and 17 (21–34), plus layers 12 and 14. No single layer has an isolated cluster, and the q×k products are spread out (the top 8 dimensions carry ≤ 0.33 of the energy). This is learned RoPE-frequency selection, so the last weight family closes without a candidate.

The overall picture from the weights: the only structural anomalies are the norm sinks. That is learned zero-gain machinery whose spectral edges explain the plateaus I found earlier. Only one sink is structurally unique: layer 4's MLP sink, the only large MLP sink, holding 33% of down_proj energy while every other MLP has ≤ 6%.

Removing the L9 attention sink was harmful, but that does not tell us about this one. If layer 4's MLP sink is a planted damper that weakens the MLP output by about 18% on every token, removing it should improve math token predictions. If it is natural calibration, removing it should cause mild broad harm, as at L9.

So I'll test it causally with one teacher-forced screen (edit E21): zero the 18 sink rows of layer-4 down_proj. Their post-FF gains are ≈ 0, so the residual write on those channels is unchanged; only the RMS damping is removed. First I drop E19 and log the plan.
